_comment: Formation-looseness-gated melee intermixing (#1094): a stationary Infantry regiment in Shield Wall (formation 4) holds ground while a LARGER Infantry regiment (40 vs 28 soldiers -- enough attackers to press hard) marches up under its own enemy-AI order and locks in melee (~tick 220). Watch the front line in the recording: the attacker presses flush against the defender's front rank and holds there. Verified via dump-state.sh (soldiers_full.pos, both units, restricted to attacker bodies that fall within the defender's own lateral frontage so a wide attacker's flanking soldiers aren't mistaken for depth-wise penetration): no attacker soldier ever crosses into the defender's own current depth span (front-edge to rear-edge Y-range) for the whole clash -- the deepest approach stays on the attacker's own side of the front rank. Compared against the pre-fix commit on this identical scenario, the regiment-level separation floor already gives Shield Wall SOME coarse protection in a clean one-on-one clash like this one, so the before/after contrast here is real but not dramatic (see the PR description for the exact numbers) -- formation_containment_margin's soldier-level guarantee matters most once that coarser mechanism's own assumptions break down (several simultaneous attackers, casualties compacting a rank), which a single clean clash doesn't stress.
